record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can adding a background potential, mirror, or active medium to a nonlinear scattering system improve the inverse problem and reduce the required data by creating extra reflected information, and can one construct a rigorous example where the S-matrix determines both the target and the added mirror while separating waves due to the nonlinearity from waves due to the background potential?

evidence.quote: Problem 4- Adding a Background Potential to a Given System Adding an extra potential or changing the background from a vacuum to something active may enhance the quality of solving the inverse problem, as well as reduce the amount of data needed Barsi et al. (2009).

The crucial point is that the S matrix also determines the mirror! Therefore, by separating (mathematically or experimentally) the waves coming from the nonlinearity and the mirror W , one gets two observations of the target from different directions, in just one measurement. A rigorous construction of such an example would be great!

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a nonlinear scattering system on $\mathbb{R}^d$ governed by an evolution equation of the form
$$ i\partial_t u + \Delta u = V(x)\, u + N(u), \qquad u(0,x)=u_0(x),$$
where $N$ is a nonlinearity supported (in a generalized sense) inside a compact "target" region $\Omega_T$, and $V$ is a linear, compactly supported "background" potential (a "mirror") with support $\Omega_M$ disjoint from $\Omega_T$. Define the scattering operator (S-matrix) $S_{V,N}:u_-\mapsto u_+$ on the space of asymptotic free states in the usual way (assuming small-data global existence and asymptotic completeness for both incoming and outgoing channels).

Address the following.

(a) Does the presence of $V$ generically reduce the amount of scattering data needed to recover $N$? That is, can one prove that for an appropriate class of nonlinearities $\{N\}$ and a fixed (or simultaneously unknown) mirror $V$, knowledge of $S_{V,N}$ on a strictly smaller set of incoming states than required when $V\equiv 0$ suffices to determine $N$ uniquely?

(b) Construct a rigorous example—specifying explicit function classes for $V$ and $N$, geometric assumptions on $\Omega_T,\Omega_M$, and a precise notion of "separation"—in which:
 (i) the scattering operator $S_{V,N}$ uniquely determines both $N$ (the target) and $V$ (the mirror);
 (ii) the outgoing wave can be decomposed (mathematically, e.g., by amplitude expansion in the small-data regime, or by frequency/time-of-flight filtering) into a "linear" component due to $V$ alone and a "nonlinear" component due to $N$;
 (iii) the two components provide two independent observations of $\Omega_T$ from distinct effective directions in a single measurement, yielding strictly more information than the $V\equiv 0$ case.

Prove or disprove the existence of such a rigorous example.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open research direction. General literature on inverse scattering transform on nontrivial backgrounds and on recovery of potentials from the S-matrix exists, but no specific result was found constructing a rigorous nonlinear scattering example where the S-matrix simultaneously determines a target nonlinearity and an added background "mirror" while cleanly separating linear and nonlinear scattering contributions. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Inverse Scattering Transform for Nonlinear Schrödinger Systems on a Nontrivial Background
status_evidence.snippet: Recent developments address IST for NLS systems on the line with physically relevant non-zero boundary conditions at space infinity.
status_evidence.claim: Inverse scattering on nontrivial backgrounds is an active area, but the specific mirror-plus-nonlinearity construction asked for is not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Inverse scattering transform - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: In the inverse scattering method, the potential is recovered from its scattering matrix.
status_evidence.claim: Standard inverse scattering recovers a potential from S, but joint recovery of an unknown nonlinearity together with an added background mirror is not standard.
